public.title: Undoable Database II
public.description: input {initial,operations}; initial is an object mapping user IDs to name strings. Draft edits put {key,value} or delete {key} emit state but do not add checkpoints. Commit checkpoints only changed drafts (compare key/value maps regardless of key order); undo/redo discard draft edits before navigating committed snapshots. A no-op commit preserves redo. Return {draft,committed} after each operation. At most 12 users and 20 operations; this represents batched database history using a key-to-name table. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.

explanation: Store committed table snapshots and a separate mutable draft. Compare maps structurally before checkpointing. O(operations times maximum table size) time and storage. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
